A_target.statement:
Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a [[Definition:Real Function|real function]] and $x_0 \in \R$.
Then $f$ is [[Definition:Continuous Real Function at Point|continuous at $x_0$]] {{iff}}:
:$\forall \epsilon > 0: \exists \delta > 0: \size {x - x_0} < \delta \implies \size {\map f x - \map f {x_0} } < \epsilon$

B_source.statement:
Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a [[Definition:Real Sequence|real sequence]] and $L \in \R$.
Then $a_n \to L$ {{iff}}:
:$\forall \epsilon > 0: \exists N \in \N: n > N \implies \size {a_n - L} < \epsilon$

validity_conditions: Both definitions share the 'challenge-response' quantifier skeleton (forall eps, exists threshold, implication on the error).
The transfer is of the proof *template* (given eps, exhibit the threshold, bound the error), not a renaming of a single structure; the threshold is found differently in each case.
proof_plan: Both definitions share the skeleton: for all $\epsilon > 0$, exhibit a threshold, then bound the error below $\epsilon$.
Map "choose $N$ such that the tail $n > N$ is close to $L$" to "choose $\delta$ such that the neighborhood $\size {x - x_0} < \delta$ is close to $\map f {x_0}$".

Given $\epsilon > 0$, construct $\delta$ from $\epsilon$ as one would construct $N$.
Then verify $\size {\map f x - \map f {x_0} } < \epsilon$ whenever $\size {x - x_0} < \delta$.

Hence an [[Definition:Epsilon-Delta Definition|$\epsilon$-$\delta$]] continuity proof follows the same plan as an $\epsilon$-$N$ proof of [[Definition:Limit of Real Sequence|convergence of a sequence]].
{{qed}}
